title: BDL Basic Circular No. 172: Cash Transaction Slip – CTS
text:
Basic Circular No. 172
To Banks and Financial Institutions
Attached is a copy of Basic Decision No. 13798 of 21 January 2026, relating to the Cash
Transaction Slip – CTS.
Beirut, 21 January 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
1

Basic Circular No. 13798
Cash Transaction Slip – CTS
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 44 of 24 November 2015 (Fighting Money
Laundering and Terrorist Financing);
Pursuant to the provisions of Basic Decision No. 7818 of 18 May 2001 (Regulations on
the Control of Financial and Banking Operations for Fighting Money Laundering and
Terrorist Financing);
Considering that Lebanon is facing, since 2019, an unprecedented systemic financial
and monetary crisis in terms of scale and severity, whose repercussions led to
fundamental changes in payment behaviors and increased reliance on cash economy;
Considering that the expansion of cash transactions poses a major risk to financial
stability, facilitates tax evasion, and increases significantly the ML/TF risk;
Considering that the Banque du Liban, based on its prerogatives that aim at
safeguarding monetary and financial stability, has taken an array of preventive,
supervisory, and regulatory measures to restore confidence and realign the Lebanese
financial sector with recognized international standards;
Considering that the Banque du Liban believes that the effective monitoring of illicit
financial flows and the reestablishment of transparency in financial operations, are two
essential prerequisites that help delisting Lebanon from the FATF “grey list”;
Considering that, to achieve these objectives, the Banque du Liban has gradually and
systematically adopted a comprehensive regulatory framework that constitutes a
protective framework for the banking and financial sector in Lebanon;
Considering that, as a fundamental first ring fence measure (RF1), the Banque du
Liban issued, on 14 November 2025, Basic Decision No. 13769 (KYC Form for Cash
Transactions and Exchange Operations) that require all non-banking financial
institutions operating in Lebanon to implement enhanced measures and comply with
KYC requirements for any cash transaction equal to, or above USD 1,000 (or its
equivalent);
Considering that the Banque du Liban, as a second ring fence measure (RF2), decided
to issue the present Basic Decision that require all banks and financial institutions
operating in Lebanon to apply stricter rules and adopt a standardized Form for cash
deposits equal to, or above, USD 10,000 or its equivalent in any other currency, on a
daily basis;
2

Considering that these two Basic Decisions constitute a dual protective system for the
Lebanese banking and financial sector, and in the same time a deterrent tool against
any funds that might be illicit or deriving from money laundering or related to terrorist
financing; and
Pursuant to the Decision of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, taken in its
meeting of 21 January 2026,
Decides the following:
Article 1:
Banks must ensure that customers complete the Cash Transaction Slip (CTS) as per attached
Form (RF2), whenever they carry out at a specific bank, on a daily basis, one or more cash
deposits equal to, or above USD 10,000 or its equivalent in any other currency.
The information provided in the CTS Form is cross-checked against the information in the
KYC Form to verify its consistency.
Article 2:
This Decision shall enter into force upon its issuance.
Article 3:
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Beirut, 21 January 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
3
